prerequisites: Translate all/no/some/some-not using the stated no-existential-import convention.
One object can belong to several sets.
Distinguish a required witness from a forbidden region.
explanation: Retain exactly the stated constraints. Do not turn all A are B into all B are A, or infer existence from a universal. Some A are B allows every A to be B as well; it does not require an A outside B. Two some statements may use different witnesses. In a finite-model check, each listed object has exactly the stated memberships and no unlisted objects exist.

worked.action: Premise: all A are B. A model with one object in A and B and another in B alone is valid.
worked.justification: Every A is in B. Nothing forbids extra B objects.

worked.action: The empty model also satisfies all A are B.
worked.justification: There is no A outside B; this convention does not infer an A witness.

worked.action: Add some A are C. Now place a witness in A,B,C.
worked.justification: The witness must be in A and C, and the universal forces it into B.

worked.action: Some A are B and some B are C can use object1 in A,B and object2 in B,C.
worked.justification: The witnesses need not be the same, so A/C overlap is not forced.

worked.action: With no A are C, that two-object model still works, while a single A,B,C witness fails.
worked.justification: Check every premise separately: satisfying the existential statements does not excuse violating a universal exclusion.

worked.action: All A are B plus no A are B permits an empty A set. Adding some A are A would make these premises inconsistent.
worked.justification: Universal constraints can empty a category; an explicit witness changes consistency.

hint: Test each premise against every listed object. For some/some-not, locate the required witness; for all/no, search for a violating object.
shortcut: Reject a proposed model as soon as one premise fails; verify every premise before accepting it.
limitation: These finite models are complete as listed and use the explicit no-existential-import convention. A valid model shows consistency, not that every feature of that model is necessary.
